title: Product
description: The product: the root of a set of specifications, with its roles and the Product extension that holds what it adds to Lathe. What every record shares (an ID, a kind, a title, a parent, header fields, links and citations) is described once, under the Product entity.

title: Test
description: A test that proves obligations or supports them, automated, manual or planned.

title: Open question
description: Something undecided, with the role that decides it. A decided question is removed and its answer written into the records it affects.

title: Standard
description: A library of engineering rules for the product's code, written once under the product beside the patterns: its rules, and the components and tests that meet them.

title: Integration
description: An outside system a domain exchanges with, and one interaction requirement per exchange.

title: Technical flow
description: How the system carries out a flow, written as ordered steps on one or more paths, each done by a component and designing the obligations it satisfies.

title: API
description: A group of endpoints for one resource, with the interaction requirements every endpoint in it shares and the shapes they share.

title: Domain
description: A part of the product with its own model, language and owner: a vertical slice of business capability, with its capabilities in order. Technology is a layer inside a domain, never a domain.

title: Aggregate
description: One aggregate of a domain, drawn as an ERD: its entities and their fields, its domain rules and the domain events it raises. Entities link with `has_one`, `has_many` and `refers_to`, which the ERD draws as edges.

title: Use case
description: Something an actor does with the product to reach a goal, with the requirements it must follow and the patterns it follows.

title: Pattern
description: Behavior several use cases share, written once under the product: its rules and the settings each following use case fills in.

title: Layer
description: An ordered part of a domain's technical specification that holds components. A product names its own layers; a component in a layer belongs to the layer's domain, and a layer changes no coverage.

title: Flow
description: A flow: an end-to-end path through views and endpoints that carries out use cases, written as ordered steps on one or more paths. A flow written as steps carries out and fulfills what its steps do, and no more.

title: View
description: A screen or page a person uses, with the interaction requirements it must follow.

title: Endpoint
description: An HTTP endpoint: its method, route, request and responses, with the interaction requirements it must follow.

title: Check
description: One rule the engine applies, as a row of the `check` table: Lathe's in `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, a product's own in its `data/check.jsonl`. Its query reads the typed tables and returns a row for each problem; the problems of a run are rows of the `problem` table, never stored.

title: Structure size
description: How many children of one kind a record may hold, and when a grouping record holds too few to be worth its level. The limit is the product's `max_children` setting; tests are grouped by what they prove, so they are never counted as one list.

title: Page
description: One place in the app, identified by its address: the products (`/`), a record at its bare ID (`/<id>`, a product's and a domain's being their overview), a group of the graph's tree (a stage or folder, `/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>`, or a record's children of one kind, `/<parent-id>/<kind>`), the checks (`/checks`), the record format (`/format`), a kind's or a check's page in it (`/format/kinds/<kind>`, `/format/checks/<check>`), or Appearance (`/settings/appearance`). App pages are lowercase words, so no ID, which starts with a capital, can take their address. Every page shows a view of one loaded workspace.
notes:
A product, domain, record or group page shows its one focus in the views that are open, each a pane: Wiki, Graph and, on a domain, aggregate or entity page, Model. The address names them, as in `?view=wiki,graph`; the views never change the path. Such a page has three columns: the navigation, the main view, and the side bar, which shows the focused record's facts. A format page has the same columns, with one pane and the kind's or check's facts in the side bar.

Spec pages only read that workspace. Records are changed in their files, by a person in an editor or by an agent, and reviewed in git.

title: Space
description: One product as a place to work in, kept apart from every other: the pages that belong to it (its Checks page among them), its icon, its place among the other spaces, and the last page visited in it. Nothing of another product shows inside a space. The current space is always the product of the page in hand.

title: Folder
description: A named, ordered group of records by kind, such as Domain model or Test plan, as the side navigation and the pages show it. Folder names and order come from the loaded workspace's meta-model, and every view reads the same folder model.

title: Graph
description: The drawing of the model: a product's tree, the nav's, laid out once as one fixed map with the product as its root in which every node has one place and one size, the groups of children of one kind, the columns they sit in, and the camera over it. Focusing a node moves the camera to frame it and the levels the depth asks for, its parent kept at the left edge; only what is in view and big enough to see is drawn, with the center's own links when asked for, and filters hide some nodes without moving the rest. The graph is a view of a page, never a place of its own.

title: Tab group
description: The pages open at once, as tabs in a row with one active, as an editor group in VS Code. Today each space has one tab group, shown at the left of the page bar above the panes (on a phone, as the Open pages sheet); later each pane could own one. The group's rules hold whatever owns it.

title: Workspace
description: The result of one load: the kinds, relation rules, records, links, problems and coverage, in the shape of `Workspace` in `lathe/src/types.ts`. A **problem** has a severity (error or warning), the check that found it, the record it is about (or none) and a message. **Coverage** is per domain and obligation kind: how many are designed (a `design` link targets them), how many are built (a component whose file exists designs them), how many are proved (an automated or manual test proves them), how many are only planned, and the gaps.

title: Panel
description: A part of the workbench a person shows, hides and resizes: the nav, the panes of a page and the side bar. Hiding a panel gives its room to the others and loses nothing.

title: Command
description: Something a person can do from anywhere in the app, with the key binding that runs it and the hints that show that binding: in the palette, the shortcuts sheet, tooltips and `aria-keyshortcuts`. Every binding and hint reads from one keymap.

title: Theme
description: How the app looks: a named set of token values, a light set and a dark set of colors, and the tokens for type, shape, density and motion that serve both. Lathe has built-in themes; a person makes their own by copying one. The person's themes, the one chosen and the Light, Dark or System choice are kept per person.

title: Control
description: One thing on a page the Reader acts on, by pointer, by keyboard or through a screen reader: a link, a button, a tab, a toggle, a field, or a box that scrolls on its own. A control has a name that holds what it shows, a target big enough to hit, a place in the keyboard's order, and never sits inside another control.

title: Product window
description: One window showing one product folder: the folder, its saved size and place, and the server it loads Lathe from, with the folders opened lately for File › Open Recent and the next launch. The page in it reaches the shell only through `window.latheDesktop`.

title: App server
description: What a window loads Lathe from: `serve()` in the shell's own process, the app's Vite dev server that the shell starts, or the owner's dev server on port 5199, which it only shares.

title: Coverage
description: What a loaded workspace counts for each domain and obligation kind: designed, built, proved and only planned, and the gaps. Every count comes from links and from tests that run, and no obligation is left out.

title: Proof claim
description: A test's claim to prove an obligation, and what its file must say to back it: the test's own ID, every ID it proves, or its key. A claim that a planned test only owes, or that counts nowhere, is named rather than hidden.

title: Pattern following
description: A domain or use case that follows a pattern, the settings it gives, and the pattern rules it owes because of that. Each following domain designs and proves the rules for itself.
